title: Dissection-Based Sex Identification in Anthopleura elegantissima
author: Elaina Berdyck

steps.title: Set up compound microscope
steps.instruction: Place the Zeiss Primo Star microscope on a stable bench, connect to power, turn on bright‑field illumination and set light intensity to a moderate level. Rotate the turret to the lowest‑power objective (10×, 0.25 NA). Place a test slide on the stage, secure with clips, and raise the stage close to the objective without contact. Use the coarse focus knob to bring the specimen into view, then the fine focus knob to sharpen the image while adjusting the condenser and iris diaphragm for optimal contrast. Increase magnification as needed by rotating to the 40× objective (0.65 NA) and refocus with the fine focus knob only.

steps.title: Set up dissecting microscope
steps.instruction: Place the Olympus SZ61 stereomicroscope on a stable bench, connect to power, and turn on the integrated illumination. Set the zoom magnification to the lowest setting. Place a test object on the stage and focus using the coarse focus knob while viewing through the eyepieces. Adjust interpupillary distance and diopter if necessary, then increase magnification as needed and refocus before beginning the dissection.

steps.title: Prepare workspace and tools
steps.instruction: Gather, clean, and lay out all dissection tools: a scalpel with a No. 22 blade, 4½‑inch dissecting scissors, a bent teasing needle, 4½‑inch straight forceps, a straight teasing needle, a wax dissecting tray (containing an anemone polyp), and fine dissection pins.

steps.title: Pin anemone polyp
steps.instruction: Place a single Anthopleura elegantissima polyp on the wax dissecting tray with the oral surface facing downward to expose the pedal disc. Secure the specimen with fine dissection pins. If debris is present on the pedal disc, gently remove it using forceps and teasing needles before proceeding.

steps.title: Open pedal disc
steps.instruction: Using the scalpel, make a small incision at the edge of the pedal disc adjacent to the top‑most pin. Insert the tips of the dissecting scissors into the incision and perform a single shallow longitudinal cut along the centre of the pedal disc, keeping cuts superficial and avoiding damage to underlying mesentery filaments. If needed, add small perpendicular cuts to aid spreading, then use additional pins to fully open and expose the mesentery filaments.

steps.title: Examine internal anatomy
steps.instruction: With a bent teasing needle and straight forceps, carefully inspect the exposed mesentery tissues and distinguish mesentery filaments, gonads, and the siphonoglyph. Begin observations with the unaided eye, then transfer the dissection tray to the dissecting microscope for higher‑magnification examination of internal structures.

steps.title: Determine sex and gonad level
steps.instruction: Assign sex (male or female) and gonad development stage by visual inspection, using a dissecting microscope at 10× or a compound microscope at 100× when necessary. Follow the gonad index:

substeps.instruction: Level 5: abundant, highly turgid, multi‑lobed gonadal masses visible to the unaided eye on most or all mesenteries.
Level 4: multi‑lobed gonadal masses visible to the unaided eye but less turgid; confident sex determination requires a dissecting microscope at 10×; gonads may not be present on all mesenteries.
Level 3: single‑lobed gonadal masses visible under a dissecting microscope at 10×; sex can be distinguished based on gonadal morphology.
Level 2: swollen mesenteries visible under a dissecting microscope; definitive sex determination requires a compound microscope at 100×.
Level 1: small discrete protrusions/bumps on mesentery filaments requiring a compound microscope at 100× for detection and sex differentiation (no specimens observed at this level in the study).

Level 0: no visible gonadal protrusions under a compound microscope at 100×; sex cannot be determined. To assess, excise a small section of mesentery with a scalpel or scissors, place it on a clean glass slide, gently apply a coverslip without excessive compression, and observe under the compound microscope. Sample multiple sections by cutting several pieces per specimen and mounting 2–3 pieces per slide or preparing multiple slides as needed to obtain a representative assessment.
